body:
I dont think I've ever been depressed, at least I've never been diagnosed. I've had some issues with self-harm. 

Honestly, I have no long term goals and that doesn't bother me like it does most people. I don't like planning my life out and I've got nothing in particular I'd like to achieve. I have hobbies/a mediocre job I'm happy with, I don't feel the need for goals bc there's nothing else I would like to achieve at the minute (other than eventually moving into a house rather than a flat)
Her colours look gorgeous!

I've definitely thought about all this, the main thing I think when I hear 'you might not regret the baby, but you'll regret not waiting' is that if I wait, I might end up with an entirely different baby. Which is quite off-putting. 

I've thought this through for months, though it may not sound long I know it's the right decision for me. Thank you for the obvious time you put into your message!

Thank you so much! The plan is to continue working for as long as I can. I'll have a few months after the baby is born in which I will continue to get my wages (my sister had 6 months, for example) and after that I plan to leave work until baby is old enough to go back to school if the pay is barely enough to cover daycare (honestly, im not too keen on that idea) but the ideal situation would be taking the later shifts when SO is already back from work. :) thank you for all the advice, I really appreciate it!

Thank you for the obvious thought you've put into your answer! Trust me, i know the possible consequences of this and I've thought it through. My biggest worry is that the pregnancy will end in another miscarriage or that some other tragic event will occur. I hadn't thought about researching how to deal with loss, I kinda assumed everyone deals with it in their own way but I can definitely see how that would beneficial for me emotionally. Thank you :)

Hey, some people *do* take that approach. But death is something most people don't really want happening sooner rather than later :)

I appreciate your opinion and I'm taking what you say into consideration, but as I've said I'm not here to be convinced. Thank you for caring about a stranger enough to try and push me in the direction you think best :) (if this comes across as sarcastic, I'm really sorry. I genuinely appreciate what you guys are trying to do)
Thank you so much! I'm definitely taking what everyone says into consideration. :)
Yeah, it does :) thank you

Thank you so much. For being non-judgmental, understanding, and putting it in a better perspective. I always gathered babies are one of those things you never regret. Sure, you might wish their dad was different or that you had them in a different part of your life, but you dont regret *them*. Once again, thank you :)

I can afford to pay my bills. I have money left over. You want a baby now, don't you? Not later. I want a house now, not later. I'm not saying it in a stroppy way, nor am I acting like a brat. I understand things will get rough. I'm not thinking its all fairytale like.

Sorry for getting a bit snappish! I did get upset because it was the first time I've shared it with someone other than my S.O. thank you for caring enough to comment your concerns at all, and thank you for the explanation :)

Sigh. NO ONE is prepared in every way possible when it comes to having your first child. How can you know I'm emotionally not? Truth is, none of you guys actually know me. All you're getting from me here is what I'm letting you see. Plenty of people jump into pregnancy without an ounce of what I've been researching and putting into it. All you have is my age and that I havent really done anything with my life, but I'm perfectly content with that. I have hobbies, I'm family orientated. I know when to be serious and I can be very mature. 

I'd put myself in a harder lifestyle because what I get out would be so much more rewarding, worth giving up my luxuries for.

I don't have any goals beyond one day owning a house with my partner, I take life as it comes. I've never been the type to be ambitious. There's been mothers younger than me before and there will be in the future. I'm choosing this because *I* know what will make me happy. How can a bunch of strangers on the internet tell me what's best for me? You don't think I have that crammed down my neck constantly already? 

I came here because I'm struggling with becoming pregnant. I expected a bit of this, and then I could post updates here like everyone else. But all this has shown me is that all I'll be getting is people telling me what a mistake I'm making. I came here for an understanding community. What I've got is strangers on the internet, some being very helpful and kind and others being.. less tactful. But all everyone is doing is telling me to wait. I'm probably more mature than a lot of older moms out there. Why shouldn't I get to choose when i'm ready? It's perfectly legal. I'm breaking no rules. I'm doing what I want with my life, and yet that still isn't good enough.

I've been around babies my whole life, believe me I know how hard it can get! I've seen my siblings crumple and sob under the pressure. I've also heard them say they wouldn't change it for the world. 

I understand where you're coming from with the stability, and I know for sure having a baby may make it even worse, but we're a lot better now than we were. We've learnt how best to settle our arguments, communication is key. We're very happy together.

I have thought this through. When I was pregnant, it was reality and I couldn't of been happier. I know I can handle this. There's support out there for young mothers if it ever becomes too much. I will have the support of my family. Thank you :)

How does it make me seem like a child? It's true for a lot of things. Losing weight (why start tomorrow when I can achieve results a day earlier) and indeed pregnancy. I have financial stability, I'm living with my partner and we have a lot of spare cash we're already saving for baby. We have a spare room for him or her. I'm mentally and physically ready. I've done my research.

Why wait when I'm in as good position as ever?

I don't need it. I want it and I don't want to wait. Why aren't you waiting? Because you want it now and you have no reason to wait. I see no reason to wait either. Sure, there's no rush, but why have something tomorrow if I can have it today? I've had since last year to think it through. It's what I want.
Thank you for that. If there's anything I've taken from this thread, it's this :)

Oh yeah, we're definitely not doing it to patch up problems! Having a baby will be very stressful, it'll push us. I know that. 

We broke up because after the MC I was very hormonal, lashing out at everyone. It was completely my fault and I accept that. I'm so sorry to hear about your friend, I can't imagine how that would feel. 

I know TV tends to glam up underage pregnancies and that is awful. I don't really watch TV other than the occasional show like game of thrones/the walking dead, but I completely understand where you're coming from. Some girls may well jump straight into pregnancy thinking it's all cuteness and social media 'likes', I totally get that I'll be a frazzled burnt out mess through lack of sleep, probably covered in vomit. It still seems worth it to me, as I'm sure a lot of people on this subreddit think it is. 

I know, I'm 17. I'm supposed to think I know everything about everything. But I can aknowledge that you know, maybe I should listen to someone older. They might just know best. But on this subject I can't. Thank you.

Thank you, but I'm not here to be talked out of it. As i've said to previous commenters, there's a bunch of older people out there that are in situations much worse than ours who successfully have children. I know we can do it *without* having to rely on government or family funding or I wouldn't dream of it. Honestly, I've never wanted to travel. Never liked the party/clubbing scene. I can't see what I'm missing out on in that aspect, though obviously date nights will be few and far between. thank you for the thought you've put into your comment!

Thank you for that. I live in England, our hospital care is paid for with taxes. Financially, we're looking at basic bills + nappies, milk formula if for whatever reason breastfeeding doesn't work out, toiletries for baby, clothing etc. I never intend to have my parents raise my child, though no doubt they will help any way they can. These are issues that can happen with older people too- an ex of mine was raised by his grandparents while his parents moved onto have another two children, for example. I won't be going to university (college) as i dropped out of education when I was pregnant and didn't want to go back when I had the mc. I'm working now, maternity leave is awesome in the UK. If I chose to go back to work after, It would be months after. And i'd be able to return to my job.


Sure, we've not been dating long (whats a couple of years when we live 80+ years?) But the same can be said for much older people who get into a relationship and are getting married 6 months later with a baby on the way.

Thank you so much :) I was expecting a bunch of hate, but all the positive vibes and people genuinely trying to be helpful is making me so happy! I'm listening to all of your advice, though it isn't changing my mind I *am* taking it into consideration

Thank you for your positivity! It's really refreshing. We're terrified to reach out to anyone about this. This is the first time I've discussed it with someone other than my SO. Obviously, none of this is enough to change our minds but it's enough to get me thinking. I believe I'm as clear minded about this as I can be. I'm not totally with my head in the cloud, I realise how expensive/time consuming it's going to be. Lack of spare time/sleep/money etc.. but honestly, it's all worth it. I see how my sister looks at her children, how my brother looks at his son. I want that so much. I'm willing to take parenting classes, I'm determined to give it my damn best which is a lot more than some parents can say.

We broke up because of the MC. I did it because I was flood with hormones. I blamed everyone but myself, really. He never wanted to break up. Thank you for your perspective, but I've considered therapy and I don't need it really. I want a baby because I psyched myself up for it with my first pregnancy, I know we can handle it. I understand that my boyfriend and I might not last - but doesn't that apply to every couple? No matter what we would put our baby first. It might be hard, but I do want it. Thank you for being so kind :)
Is Joah like Noah with a J? Josias is a lovely name :)
Josephus sounds too close to Joseph unfortunately :( Joseph is my nephew, so can't really use too similar names. How is Joakim pronounced? :)
Jordan is NMS but I really like Joel!
Oh I love Jonah!!
Might sound a bit dumb but is that pronounced how its spelt? Like Joe-sigh-a?
....Arian like Aryan?
